new.n: David B. Stillman's missing gold hoard, near Shiocton
new.pl: Shiocton-area circle, town of Bovina; the son's farm where he lived has not been placed on a plat. Pin is the village, not the farm.
new.st: David B. Stillman, an old farmer who distrusted banks, died in March 1910 at a son's home in the town of Bovina near Shiocton, where he had lived since about 1892 after selling his own 40 acres near Black Creek. A neighbour who later administered the estate had counted more than $5,000 in gold for him. He kept it in a can under the floor, in the woodshed and wood piles, and in spots buried in the yard that he watered so the grass would grow over them as a marker. Only about $600-700 was found after his death. In December 1910 the probate court questioned the sons about the rest; the heirs accused two of them of concealing it, and the papers reported that the hidden gold had not been found. The estate closed in January 1911 with a residue of $547.77. His former farm near Black Creek, sold years earlier, is not the cache site.
new.t: Lead grade C: two local papers and the probate file agree a hoard of about $5,000 existed and about $4,300 went missing; it may have been taken rather than left in the ground. Find the son's farm near Shiocton on an 1889 or 1928 Bovina plat before any visit. Private farmland: permission.
